script: Growing your own vegetables is easier than most people think. You do not need a big garden. A sunny balcony and a few large pots are enough to start. Choose easy plants first, like tomatoes, chillies, spinach and mint. Fill each pot with good soil mixed with compost, and make sure there are holes at the bottom so extra water can drain away. Plant the seeds about as deep as twice their size, then water them gently. Most vegetables need at least five hours of direct sunlight every day, so place the pots where the light is strongest. Water in the early morning or the evening, when the sun is not too hot. Check the leaves every few days for insects, and remove them by hand. In a few weeks, you will see the first flowers, and soon after, your first harvest. Save a few seeds from your best plants for next season, and share the extra harvest with your neighbours. Gardening also teaches patience, because every plant grows at its own pace. There is nothing quite like eating a tomato you grew yourself.
